title: Reflexion: Part 1 - Replacing Weight Updates with Verbal RL

beats.text: Why is Reflexion a major breakthrough? Because large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly used to interact with external environments (e.g., games, compilers, APIs) as goal-driven agents.

The core challenge? However, it remains challenging for these language agents to quickly and efficiently learn from trial-and-error as traditional reinforcement learning methods require extensive training samples and expensive model fine-tuning.
beats.visual_focus: Bottleneck diagram illustrating resource contention and latency walls.

beats.text: Enter Reflexion: Enter Reflexion: Part 1 - Replacin: Reflexion, a novel framework to reinforce language agents not by updating weights, but instead through linguistic feedback.

beats.text: Under the hood, concretely, Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals, then maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials.

beats.text: The result? Reflexion is flexible enough to incorporate various types (scalar values or free-form language) and sources (external or internally simulated) of feedback signals, and obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks (sequential decision-making, coding, language reasoning).
